extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance drawn from PTAB decisions on drafting claims and specifications to survive 35 U.S.C. §101 rejections (integrating judicial exceptions into practical applications, claiming improvements to technology/computers, and amending claims post-appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure a variety of method and device claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure a variety of method and device claims to allow the best chances of some claims surviving a 101 rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device claims (e.g., devices 'configured to' perform steps) may be viewed as 'special-purpose improved machines' and more likely to be treated as more than a generic computer, whereas method claims may be seen as mental processes; diversify claim types to maximize survivability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize improvement to a computer or computer component
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize in applications and reflect in claims improvement to a computer or computer component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A different formulation or additional description of claimed devices could frame method claims as closer to cases like McRO or Enfish (i.e., showing how the invention improves the operation of a physical display or other computer component).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claims that can be performed in the human mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed towards a process that can be performed in the human mind will likely not be found patent eligible by PTAB (as well as Federal Circuit) unless Applicant adds specific elements directed to an improvement in computer technology or the particular technology field or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Guidance, 'determining' steps that can be practically performed mentally (or with pen and paper/lookups) fall into the 'mental process' grouping; see MPEP 2106.05(a) for related USPTO guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make data-analysis/determining steps non-manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims focused on 'determining' or other data-analysis steps should emphasize and claim specific elements that support the inability to perform those steps manually or in the human mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such specific elements should be supported in the Specification to emphasize the unique advantages of performing the steps through software for the particular technology field or technological process (e.g., golf club fitting technology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight technical innovations in specification and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should emphasize and highlight any technical innovations in the invention, both in the specification and the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the Specification and claims to support a technical solution to a technical problem; tie algorithmic or analytic steps to particular technological benefits and uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Directed to' and 'inventive concept' prongs can overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'directed to' and 'inventive concept' prongs of the Guidance can be overlapping in analysis, even if considered separately by the Examiner or the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counseling clients or amending claims, be aware that arguments/evidence may simultaneously bear on both prongs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of a database or processor is insufficient alone
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere presence of a database or a processor here does not necessarily indicate a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB viewed a processor 'merely used to perform calculations' and a database that 'merely stores the results' as insufficient token elements; broad 'measuring' steps and generic storage/processing do not integrate an abstract idea into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional elements must be more than well-understood, routine, conventional
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional elements must provide more than well-understood, routine, and conventional functionality; otherwise they do not provide an inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that are an 'abstract-idea-based solution implemented with generic technical components in a conventional way' will be held ineligible under the Guidance's inventive-concept analysis (Step 2B).

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'technological arts' test
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no 'technological arts' test for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex Parte Lundgren reversed an Examiner for using an improper 'technological arts' test; practitioners should not rely on that test as the basis for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recite concrete device interactions and machine steps when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that include specific device interactions (e.g., scanning by a second device, identifying via machine-readable code, delivering formatted results between devices) can support a finding that the claims are not directed to an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board found claims that recited concrete steps performed by multiple devices and automated processing to identify lab tests were not directed to an abstract idea, even where underlying technologies were generic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show improvement to technology for human-interaction claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims involving human interactions or managing personal behavior must show an improvement to technology; transformation of information alone will not suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB held that sharing content among persons fit within an abstract idea (managing personal behavior/relationships) and that merely transforming information or using generic technology does not integrate the idea into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate mathematical concepts into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that recite mathematical concepts should recite additional elements that integrate the mathematical concepts into a practical application (e.g., specific physical steps or particular machine use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reciting steps of placing a tool on an organ surface, associating positions with a 3D image, and generating mapping functions using thin plate splines to improve catheter navigation demonstrated integration (improving registration and reducing localization errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recite implementation details of algorithms and surrounding technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should recite surrounding technology and implementation details of the algorithm to ensure it is viewed as a 'practical application' of those concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications should likewise highlight the benefits to the technology and specific uses of any mathematical concepts within the technology so that the algorithm is shown as applied to a technological problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper incorporation of technology into claims avoids 'well-understood' debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper incorporation of technology into claims can render the claims a 'practical application' and avoid getting into a debate over whether that technology is 'well-understood' as part of the inventive concept step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are drafted to integrate and apply the technology meaningfully, the PTAB/Examiner may deem the claim an eligible application of the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'configured to' and structural limitations to claim special-purpose machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'configured to' device language and add structural limitations to claim special-purpose improved machines rather than generic processors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB found device claims 'configured to' perform steps were persuasive as 'special-purpose improved machines'; adding structural and specific method limitations post-appeal led to allowance in an example case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend claims post-appeal to add structural/specific method limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-appeal claim amendments adding structural limitations and specific method limitations directed towards an improvement to the technology can lead to allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after adding such limitations directed to improvement in golf fitting technology, the Examiner allowed the application, noting the amendments integrated the abstract idea into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processor limitations must show technical solution to technical problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Processor limitations that only perform mental/calculational tasks are insufficient; claims should show how the processor contributes to a technical solution to a technical problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB criticized processors 'merely used to perform calculations' when those calculations could be done mentally; claims should instead recite how the processor improves measurement, manufacturing, or other technical operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation or reduction of an article is an indicia of integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformation and reduction of an article are indicia of integration into a practical application; absence of such indicia weighs against eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB reviewed indicia of integration (e.g., transformation of an article) and concluded none were present in some cases where claims were held abstract.
